Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the forecasts compared to true outcomes.

Looking at the data, I can see this is EU ETS (carbon market) price forecasting with 30-day ahead forecasts vs actual outcomes.

Let me examine the patterns:

## Example 1 (2025-11-11)
- History starts at 79.51 and moves around 79-80 range
- Sentiment ranges from 0.00 to 1.00
- Model forecasts are around 80.43 on day 1, 81.33 on day 2, etc.
- True outcomes: 80.65, 81.91, 81.34, 80.93, 79.92, 81.22, 80.66, 81.36, 80.41, 80.61, 81.87, 81.68, 82.21, 83.26, 82.64, 81.82, 81.79, 82.43, 81.98, 81.98, 82.85, 82.42, 83.90, 83.79, 87.28, 87.36, 86.80, 86.48, 87.05, 87.48

## Example 2 (2025-11-10)
- Very similar to Example 1 but forecast is slightly different
- True outcomes are essentially the same starting from day 1

## Example 3 (2025-11-07)
- Slightly different history (first price is 79.45 vs 80.43)
- Forecasts and outcomes are very similar to Example 1

## Example 4 (2025-11-06)
- First forecast is 80.41 vs 80.43 in Example 1
- Outcomes are the same

## Example 5 (2025-11-05)
- First forecast is 81.68 vs 80.43 in Example 1


- Outcomes begin at 81.49, showing a subtle divergence from previous comparisons

I notice the forecasts are consistently underestimating the true outcomes, particularly as the horizon extends. The model seems to struggle with capturing the full magnitude of price movements, especially in the early days. Sentiment signals mixed emotions, ranging from cautious optimism to uncertainty, which might complicate the forecasting approach.
